title: When the Salt Wakes
premise: Paloma Thackeray has spent her life in the valley of Vell, where magic cannot follow, serving as royal food-taster to a court that values her only for her poison-proof body. When a mute child arrives speaking the dead language of Ostrava—a kingdom erased from every map and memory—Paloma begins to understand the words, because her grandmother's lullabies were the same tongue. The child is a living key: the door out of vanished Ostrava still exists inside the valley's salt caves, and it will close forever at the winter solstice. Paloma must choose between the found family she built in Vell and the inheritance she never knew she carried, ultimately holding the door open long enough for the last exiles of Ostrava to pass through—then walking back into the valley, changed but not gone.
about_author: Paloma Almeida grew up between her grandmother's kitchen and her grandfather's shipping maps, and writes about people who belong to more than one place. She lives near the coast, where she keeps an unexplained collection of keys that open nothing—yet.

chapters.title: The Taster's Tongue
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. A morning of tasting for the suspicious Queen Regent establishes Paloma's routine, her immunity earned dish by dish, and her careful invisibility among court servants. Emotional beat: quiet loneliness disguised as competence.

chapters.title: Salt on the Threshold
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. On her rare day off, she finds a child, six or seven years old, standing at her cottage door caked in white salt, unafraid. The child speaks a language Paloma doesn't recognize—and yet her mouth shapes an answer before her mind consents. Beat: uncanny recognition.

chapters.title: Lullaby in a Dead Tongue
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV, with flashback. The child sleeps; Paloma hums her grandmother's lullaby and realizes, horrified, that the syllables match. She digs out her grandmother's recipe book and finds marginalia in the same script. Beat: inheritance surfacing.

chapters.title: What the Valley Cannot Hold
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. She consults old Hedda, the herbalist, who explains the valley's founding: magic cannot cross its borders, which is why refugees like Paloma's grandmother came here. Hedda goes pale at the child's name-sound. Beat: dread taking root.

chapters.title: The Court Summons
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. The Queen Regent's spymaster, Corvane, notices Paloma's absences and summons her early. She tastes, survives a subtle poison meant for someone else, and realizes Corvane is watching her now. Beat: safety fraying.

chapters.title: A Name Like Water
chapters.summary: Child's POV, rendered in simple sensory prose. We learn the child's name—Issel—and fragments of why they crossed into the valley: something following, something closing. Beat: innocence carrying terrible weight.

chapters.title: Recipes as Maps
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Deciphering her grandmother's marginalia, Paloma realizes the recipes are coded directions—the salt caves beneath the valley are described like ingredients. Beat: wonder sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: Corvane's Kindness
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Corvane offers protection, patronage, even warmth—but asks about strangers at her door. Paloma lies for the first time in her careful life. Beat: the cost of belonging to two truths.

chapters.title: Found Family, Small Hours
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Issel and Paloma build a fragile domestic rhythm: teaching each other words over soup. Neighbors begin leaving food at the door. Beat: tenderness amid danger.

chapters.title: The First Sign
chapters.summary: Hedda's POV. Salt blooms where no sea has ever been—in Hedda's well, in the church font. The valley itself is reacting to Issel's presence. Beat: the world tilting.

chapters.title: Into the Caves
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Following the recipe-map, Paloma takes Issel into the salt caves and finds a wall that hums when Issel touches it. Carved around it: a language older than kingdoms. Beat: awe and fear entwined.

chapters.title: The Door That Isn't There
chapters.summary: Issel's POV. Issel shows Paloma how the door appears only to those who carry Ostravan blood—and Paloma's hand passes through light. She is not merely descended from Ostrava; she is one of its last. Beat: identity overturned.

chapters.title: Winter Court
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Back at court, solstice preparations begin. Corvane presents his theory to the Regent: magic is leaking through the valley's border, and a taster's family may be the cause. Beat: hunted.

chapters.title: The Exile's Ledger
chapters.summary: Hedda's POV. Hedda reveals she was born outside the valley too, and produces a ledger of refugee families—including 'Thackeray,' altered from an Ostravan name. Beat: grief for a hidden lineage.

chapters.title: Running Out of Days
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Paloma calculates the solstice deadline from the cave inscriptions. The door opens once per generation; miss it, and Ostrava's survivors outside are sealed away forever. Beat: clock starting.

chapters.title: Issel Speaks
chapters.summary: Issel's POV. Trauma loosens: Issel finally speaks—in Paloma's grandmother's dialect—describing the hunters called the Grey Choir who erase countries and chase survivors. Beat: catharsis and terror.

chapters.title: A Poison of Her Own
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Corvane tests Paloma with a poisoned dish; her immunity saves her, but he confirms what she is. He gives her three days to surrender the child. Beat: betrayal wearing a friendly face.

chapters.title: The Neighbors' Net
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. The valley's small community—baker, ferryman, Hedda—conspire to hide Issel, each risking their precarious belonging. Beat: found family made literal.

chapters.title: Grey Choir at the Border
chapters.summary: Issel's POV. Issel senses the Choir reaching the valley's edge, unable to enter but patient, singing the valley's name wrong until it frays. Beat: siege atmosphere.

chapters.title: What Belonging Costs
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Paloma confronts the Regent privately, offering her resignation and service in exchange for letting the child go. The Regent, herself an outsider once, hesitates. Beat: moral complexity.

chapters.title: The Ferryman's Debt
chapters.summary: Ferryman Bram's POV. Bram owes Paloma's grandmother his life; he agrees to move them by night along the underground river toward the caves. Beat: debts of kindness across generations.

chapters.title: Choir Song Rising
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The valley's animals flee; salt frost creeps inward. The Choir's song becomes audible to everyone now. Beat: collective dread.

chapters.title: Hedda's Choice
chapters.summary: Hedda's POV. Hedda stays behind to mislead Corvane, knowing she'll be imprisoned. Her farewell to Paloma reframes inheritance: not blood alone, but what you carry forward. Beat: sacrifice.

chapters.title: Underground River
chapters.summary: Paloma and Issel's POV, alternating. The boat journey through glowing salt caverns; quiet conversation about whether Paloma would leave the valley if the door opened fully. Beat: intimacy under pressure.

chapters.title: The Door Remembers
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. At the humming wall, Paloma reads the full inscription via her grandmother's key-phrase: the door leads to Ostrava-as-it-was, preserved, holding its last citizens in stasis. Beat: scale of stakes revealed.

chapters.title: Issel's Secret
chapters.summary: Issel's POV. Issel confesses: they weren't sent to find help—they were sent because a door needs a key on both sides, and Issel is the inside half. If Issel returns, they cannot come back out. Beat: heartbreak.

chapters.title: Refusal
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Paloma refuses to deliver a child to permanent exile and resolves to find another way: open the door without sending Issel through. Beat: defiance of fate.

chapters.title: Corvane Arrives
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. Corvane, guided by captured Hedda's false trail—or true one?—reaches the caves with soldiers. His motive complicates: he lost family to a vanished land too. Beat: enemy humanized.

chapters.title: Standoff in the Salt
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Negotiation collapses; the Choir's song breaches the valley border as the door weakens it. Soldiers panic. Beat: chaos erupting.

chapters.title: The Choir Enters
chapters.summary: Issel's POV. The Grey Choir pours into the caverns, faceless singers unmaking color and memory as they advance. Beat: horror peak.

chapters.title: Taste of Ash
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Cornered, Paloma realizes her lifelong poisoning has made her something the Choir's unmaking cannot grip—a body accustomed to small deaths. She walks into their song and it falters. Beat: her curse becomes power.

chapters.title: The Key Is a Meal
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. The door doesn't need Issel sacrificed—it needs a shared meal, an act of hospitality, the oldest Ostravan rite. Paloma cooks from her grandmother's book in the dark. Beat: domesticity as salvation.

chapters.title: Solstice Opening
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. At the exact solstice minute, the door opens: light, music, a city suspended in amber evening. Ostravan faces peer out. Beat: transcendent wonder.

chapters.title: Crossings
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Exiles emerge; some valley folk choose to go; Corvane, weeping, sends his memories of his lost homeland through instead of himself. Beat: bittersweet exchange.

chapters.title: Issel's Decision
chapters.summary: Issel's POV. Given the choice, Issel chooses to stay with Paloma—choosing found family over returning home. The door accepts, reshaping its terms. Beat: agency reclaimed.

chapters.title: Closing the Door
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Paloma holds the door as the last exiles pass, then seals it with the final recipe—a pinch of valley salt, a promise kept. The Choir, purpose spent, dissolves. Beat: costly triumph.

chapters.title: Aftermath in Vell
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Return to the court: the Regent grants Paloma a new role as keeper of records for vanished lands; Hedda is freed; the valley's magic-seal is permanently softened. Beat: reckoning and reward.

chapters.title: Two Names, One Table
chapters.summary: Domestic ensemble scene. Paloma cooks a feast blending both cuisines; neighbors, soldiers, and Issel crowd the cottage. Issel teaches the first Ostravan word to valley children. Beat: belonging remade, wider than before.

chapters.title: The Lullaby Continued
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV, quiet night. Paloma adds her own verse to her grandmother's lullaby and sings it to sleeping Issel in both languages. Beat: inheritance transformed into gift.

chapters.title: When the Salt Wakes
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Paloma's POV. Years later, faint salt blooms again at the valley's edge—not threat, but greeting: somewhere, Ostrava remembers them. Paloma wakes Issel to see it. Final beat: doors, once truly opened, never wholly close.
